notes: §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR5 reads "The punctuation character quotation mark is a separator", requires the opening one to be "immediately preceded by a space, left parenthesis, or opening pseudo-text delimiter" and the closing one to be "immediately followed by one of the separators space, comma, semicolon, period, right parenthesis, or closing pseudo-text delimiter". The adjacency half conforms at 85: SeparatorRule.Violations (run over every token by Frontend.LexAndParseOnce, edition-invariant) asks OpeningDelimiterSeparated and ClosingDelimiterSeparated of each literal token and reports COBOL2633; probes refused DISPLAY"HI", S"A", ="ABCDEF", "A"S, "ABCDEF"OR and "A","B" (with COBOL2631 for the comma) and accepted a literal after a left parenthesis, before a right parenthesis, comma-space, semicolon-space and period, and inside ==...== of a REPLACE. The delimiter half does not: the row's change record names the 2023 difference as §2023:8.3.5 5), "Either an apostrophe or a quotation mark may be used as the quotation symbol character in opening and closing delimiters", and the compiler applies that sentence at every edition. The lexer fragment STR_BODY takes an apostrophe as an opening and closing delimiter, and LiteralScreen.GateFormat, the one edition screen of a literal's written form, gates X"..." (COBOL0900 at 85, probed; N"..." and B"..." are refused with their classes) and the zero-length literal and has no arm for the apostrophe, so at --std 85 an apostrophe-delimited literal is a separator-delimited literal. The witness is DISPLAY"HI", refused at 85. Same mechanism and one fix with row 1985-FMT-IV.4.2.2.2.1.1 (the nonnumeric literal's format); no kb/Work note owns it.

next.reason: Amendment X3.23b-1993 rewrote the rule: 'An opening quotation mark must be immediately preceded by a space, left parenthesis, or opening pseudo-text delimiter', the closing one followed by 'space, comma, semicolon, period, right parenthesis, or closing pseudo-text delimiter', and the adjoining separators 'are not part of' the quotation-mark separators (§1985:IV.4.2.1 SR5). §2023:8.3.5 SR5 now states those adjacency rules word for word ('The opening delimiter shall be immediately preceded by a space, left parenthesis, or opening pseudo-text delimiter'), so the pseudo-text difference the withdrawn record quoted is gone. What still differs is the set of delimiters: 1985 'The punctuation character quotation mark is a separator'; 2023 'Either an apostrophe or a quotation mark may be used as the quotation symbol character in opening and closing delimiters', and its opening delimiters include the two-character forms B, N or X followed by the quotation symbol and the three-character forms BX or NX followed by it. An apostrophe-delimited literal, and a quotation mark directly preceded by B, N, X, BX or NX (refused by 'must be immediately preceded by a space, left parenthesis, or opening pseudo-text delimiter'), are accepted: new syntax, so CHANGED.
